newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR ENDS STEADY TO SOFTER.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR ENDS STEADY TO SOFTER.

text.p: The Zimbabwe dollar, which dealers were predicting would start recovering after two weeks of relentless import pressure, failed to do so on Monday after an unexpected intervention by the central bank to mop up excess foreign currency.

"We had expected the dollar to start stabilising -- at one point some people were quoting 10.1800/2300 -- but surprisingly the Reserve Bank came into the market, buying at the 10.3000 level and people are now quoting wide spreads again," one dealer said.
"Maybe they (central bank) just don't want to see the dollar appreciate," he added.
Reserve Bank officials were not available for comment.
Dealers maintained that the market had shrugged off a nationwide strike by civil servants demanding salary increments.

They said the outcome of a cabinet meeting on Tuesday to decide the fate of those civil servants who had defied a government order to go back to work or face dismissal was also unlikely to have any effect.
"Ours is just a demand and supply market," one dealer explained on Monday morning.

At the close of interbank trade, the Zimbabwe dollar was quoted at 10.2500/3500 against the key U.S. unit, from Friday's 10.2500/3000 and weakened to 16.0000/1700 from 15.9640/16.0500 versus sterling.
It was at 6.9100/9800 from 6.9110/9470 against the mark while against the rand it finished at 2.2900/3150 compared to 2.2850/2980 on Friday afternoon.
